issues.description: The solution implementation declares lecture attributes using snake_case names (e.g., lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students) but the constructor and methods use camelCase names (e.g., lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents). This mismatch means the solution code will not compile and contradicts the attribute names shown in the problem UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, etc.), causing confusion for students about the intended field names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute names consistent. Either rename the declared fields in the solution to use the camelCase names shown in the UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) or adjust the constructor and all method references to use the snake_case field names. Prefer aligning to the UML/problem statement (camelCase) so template, problem statement and solution use the same identifiers.

issues.description: The problem statement (UML) specifies attribute names in camelCase (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). In the solution implementation the attributes are declared with snake_case (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) while the rest of the solution (constructor, getters/setters, toString, and methods) uses camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, ...). This creates a mismatch between the problem specification and the solution and an internal inconsistency inside the solution file itself, which will confuse students trying to map the UML and task description to the concrete implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make identifier names consistent: use the camelCase attribute names from the UML (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) in the solution implementation (change declared field names to camelCase), and ensure all constructor parameters and method bodies reference the same camelCase fields. Alternatively, if snake_case is intentionally preferred, update the problem statement and all usages to match that choice consistently.
